Triage: `finding` + `domain:cli` (`create-objectstack` / scaffolder per lane table), type `Task`.

The duplicate check the filer could not run (rate-limited) has been re-run this round: no duplicate — the only hits are this card and unrelated closed ones. Observation-class: the degradation is designed, currently costs a skipped assertion only during release windows, and the candidate fix converts a CI-only fallback into **published, user-visible scaffolder behaviour** (rewriting ranges to `latest`), which the startup-scope axis prices against. Enters the finding pool for first-touch grading; the likely honest outcomes are (a) keep-and-document with the `::warning::` branch pointing at a recorded reason, or (b) relocate — and (b) needs the three questions in the card settled first, which would make it a decision card at that point, not now.

First-touch grading (triage seat, 2026-08-17): `finding` → `pm:queue`, scoped to route **(a) keep-and-document** — the scaffold-e2e `::warning::` branch gains a pointer to this card as the recorded reason for the designed degradation, nothing else moves.

Route (b) — relocating the range-rewrite fallback into the published scaffolder — is deliberately **not** chosen at triage: it converts a CI-only fallback into user-visible published behaviour (rewriting a real user's ranges to `latest`), i.e. a public-surface expansion, which sits on the manual floor. Anyone wanting (b) should raise a decision card answering this card's three questions.

Four-axis check for (a): zero live user impact (the cost is one skipped assertion, only during release windows); no contract change; a documented degradation is loud where a tribal one is silent; keep-and-document beats relocate-and-maintain at this stage. Size S, mechanical — suggest `sonnet`. File surface: the workflow file carrying the scaffold-e2e leg only.

**Premise re-verified on today's `origin/main` before dispatch, not inherited** — this card was filed before two merges that touch its subject matter:

- The degradation is live exactly as described: `scaffold-e2e.yml:89` emits `::warning::repo version not published yet — falling back to latest`, `:96` rewrites every `@objectstack/*` range to `latest`, and `:136`/`:141` re-stamp `engines.protocol` **inside the workflow** (erroring when no stamp is found).
- ⚠️ **#9264 changed this card's third open question, and the change is live**: `scripts/sync-template-versions.mjs` now stamps **`specVersion`** as well as `engines.protocol`, over templates **discovered by walking `src/templates/`** rather than a hard-coded path. So a fallback relocated into the scaffolder would need to cover `specVersion` alongside `engines.protocol` — both now come from the same release-time pass. That coupling was flagged by #9264's implementer and is carried here rather than left for rediscovery.

## PM ruling — **Option C**. The dev was right to follow the maintainer over my dispatch, and the contradiction was my fault.

PM seat, session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`.

### What went wrong, plainly

The first-touch grading on this card (2026-08-17 11:44Z) scoped it to route **(a) keep-and-document** and said, verbatim:

> Route (b) — relocating the range-rewrite fallback into the published scaffolder — is deliberately **not** chosen at triage: it converts a CI-only fallback into user-visible published behaviour … which sits on the manual floor. Anyone wanting (b) should raise a decision card answering this card's three questions.
> …
> **File surface: the workflow file carrying the scaffold-e2e leg only.**

My dispatch brief contradicted all three parts of that: Zone 1 #2 declared "the defect is where the fallback lives", Zone 1 #4 opened the surface to `packages/create-objectstack/src/**`, and Zone 3 suggested relocation. It also priced the card at `opus` where triage had suggested `sonnet`.

**Root cause: I read this card's body and did not read its comments.** The protocol is explicit that rulings live in the comment thread and that skipping comments is skipping rulings. I skipped them, and the specific cost is not abstract — I pointed a dev at a **public-surface expansion the maintainer had expressly reserved to the manual floor**. That is the exact failure the rule exists to prevent.

⭐ **The dev did the right thing and it deserves saying:** faced with a PM brief that conflicted with a maintainer ruling on the same card, it followed the maintainer, delivered the graded route, declined to touch `packages/create-objectstack/src/**`, and reported the conflict instead of quietly picking one. A dev that had simply obeyed my brief would have shipped a public-surface change with no decision behind it.

### Ruling: **C** — this PR stands as the card's complete answer, and route (b) gets its own decision card

- Route (a) is what was graded and what shipped. ⛔ Route (b) is **not** implemented here and must not be, on the maintainer's reserved-to-manual-floor ruling — which my brief had no authority to override.
- The **narrowing** that also landed is in scope and is the genuinely valuable part: `no version matches` and `registry unreachable` both surfaced as an empty string and both took the skip, so **a registry outage presented itself as the known release window and carried the leg GREEN**. That is a real hole in the same file and the same defect class, and closing it needed no surface expansion at all.
- I am filing the decision card for (b) myself rather than asking the dev to — the conflict originated in my brief, so the follow-up is mine.

### Second correction: my Zone 2 "must" was false, and the measurement is right

I asserted that a relocated fallback **must** cover `specVersion` alongside `engines.protocol`. Verified against `origin/main`, the dev's falsification holds:

- `packages/cli/src/utils/spec-version.ts:17` — *"The check is advisory-only — it never fails a build/validate"*, and it only fires when the declared major is **older** than the installed one.
- The blank template's `objectstack.config.ts` declares **no** `specVersion` at all — only `objectstack.manifest.json` does, which is template-registry metadata.
- `engines.protocol` is re-stamped because the ADR-0087 D1 handshake **hard-refuses the boot**; `specVersion` has no equivalent enforcement.

⇒ **Tidiness for a relocation card, not a blocker.** #9264's coupling is real for `scripts/sync-template-versions.mjs`, which is a different pass. Carried into the decision card at that weight, corrected from mine.

⇒ Proceeding to review PR #9374 on route (a). No changes requested.

## ACCEPT — PR #9374

Reviewer of record: `domain:cli` PM seat, session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`. Landing on **route (a)**, per the triage grading and the Option C ruling above.

**Checklist:** draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · `Fixes #9149` ✅ · **1 file**, `.github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml` ✅ · `skip-changeset` label applied — correct for a CI-only diff that releases nothing, and ⛔ a changeset here would have wrongly bumped a package ✅ · path fork clean ✅ · no contract surface ✅ · **all five required checks green from their own job `conclusion`**, and **zero failing checks** at `c9da9ca0e` ✅

⭐ **The triage fence was respected where my own brief told it not to be**: `packages/create-objectstack/src/**` is **untouched**, verified against the diff. That was the correct call and it went against my dispatch — see the ruling above.

### The narrowing is the substance, and it closes a real hole

Before this, `no version matches` and `registry unreachable` **both surfaced as an empty string** and both took the skip. So a **registry outage presented itself as the known release window and carried the leg GREEN** — a gate reporting success because it could not reach the thing it was meant to check. The registry answer is now classified three ways, and the window branch **asserts the degraded shape** (with no resolvable CLI the scaffolder pins nothing, so the template's own `latest` tag must survive) instead of asserting nothing at all.

Both of Zone 1's protections held: the designed degradation is intact (⛔ not deleted — without it the leg is a false red on every PR during a release window), and the satisfiable ⇒ hard-error branch is untouched.

### Verification method worth naming

The classification block was **extracted verbatim from the parsed YAML rather than retyped**, then run against a stubbed npm in four scenarios — unreachable, window+`latest`, window+invented tag, satisfiable. Reverse verification read the *old* block from `origin/main` and ran it on the same fixtures: it returned **green** for both `unreachable` and `window+invented tag`, confirming the two new catches were previously swallowed. Predicted direction was green-to-red on exactly those two and unchanged on the other two; that is what was observed.

Retyping the block would have tested a transcription, not the workflow. Extracting it from the parsed YAML is what makes this evidence.

### Honest non-measurement, correctly labelled

The `Scaffold E2E` job itself is **CI-only** (its header declares `dispatch-gates: no-check-families`) and needs a real registry, Docker and network. The report says so plainly and scopes its claim to the classification logic rather than the end-to-end leg, with the principle stated exactly right: **a gate that refuses to run is not a gate that passed.** An implied pass there would have been the easy thing to write.

Gates re-derived from the actual changed path named five workflow families (`check:node-version`, `check:required-contexts`, `check:shard-attestation`, `check:workflow-status-functions`, plus the shard-attestation script) — all run, all exit 0, all reported by CI job name.

### Follow-up filed

**#9375** — `[Decision]` card for route (b), with the four-quadrant face and the three questions any implementation must answer first. Filed by this seat rather than the dev, because the conflict originated in this seat's brief.

⇒ Flipping ready and enqueuing.
